zh: 固定较大的下标 j，合法的 i 就是此前出现过、且等于“fruits[j] 零次或一次交换两个数位后所得整数”的那些位置。一个最多 10 位的数，只有至多 45 种交换。
从左到右扫描，用哈希表记录已出现各数值的次数。对当前数 y，生成它零次或一次交换可达的全部整数（去重！重复数字可能交换出同一个值），把这些值在表中的次数加到答案，再把 y 自己记入表中。
生成候选时把数字串交换后按普通整数解析，前导零自动消失（例如 1000 首尾交换得到 1）；交换结果可能超过 32 位，用 64 位整数。不要把“数字多重集相同”当作可达——一次交换只能改变两个位置。总时间约 O(N·45)。
en: Fix the larger index j: the valid i are earlier positions whose value equals some integer obtained from fruits[j] with zero or one swap of two digit positions. A number with at most 10 digits has at most 45 swaps.

Scan from left to right and keep a hash map of how often each value has appeared. For the current number y, generate every integer reachable with zero or one swap, deduplicate them (repeated digits can produce the same value), add their counts from the map to the answer, and only then record y itself.

When generating candidates, parse the swapped digit string as an ordinary integer so leading zeros vanish (1000 with its ends swapped becomes 1); results can exceed 32 bits, so use 64-bit integers. Do not treat "same multiset of digits" as reachable, since one swap changes only two positions. The total work is about O(N * 45).

explanationEn:
## Approach

Enumerate from left to right the number `y` at the larger index. Swap zero times or swap any one pair of positions in the decimal digits of `y` to get all reachable integers. Look up how many times each reachable integer appeared before and add these counts; then add `y` to the frequency table. The reachable set must be deduplicated, to avoid counting twice when repeated digits produce the same target value.

After a swap, compare as integers; if the digit string starts with zeros, ignore the leading zeros as in reading an ordinary decimal integer. For example, swapping the first and last digits of `1000` gives `0001`, which corresponds to the integer `1`.

## Correctness

Fix the right index `j`. The source problem allows only zero or one swap on `fruits[j]`, so the enumerated position pairs generate exactly all legal target integers. The frequency table contains only elements with `i<j`, so adding the candidate frequencies counts exactly all valid left indices; deduplicating the set ensures each index pair is counted once. Iterating over every `j` gives the full answer.

## Complexity

At most 10 digits, so each number checks at most 45 position pairs. Time `O(N*D^2)` and space `O(N+D^2)`, where `D<=10`.

## Source and site conventions

The fixed FastPrep text explicitly requires `i<j`, allows swapping at most two digits, and explicitly counts no swap. The original implementation grouped numbers by their sorted digits, which miscounts permutations that need multiple swaps; this problem is implemented independently from the statement. The source gives only the function signature, and this site adds standard input and output; results are compared as integers, so leading zeros are not kept.
